rows: Digestive – GERD, oesophageal spasm, peptic disease
Emotional/endocrine – panic-related symptoms, thyrotoxicosis-related demand ischaemia

blocks.title: **Clinical application:** When evaluating chest pain, first exclude immediately life-threatening causes:

blocks.text: **Exam pearl:** Crushing central chest pain radiating to the left arm or jaw suggests myocardial ischaemia, but atypical presentations are common, particularly in older people and people with diabetes.
Additional important causes include cardiomyopathy, myocarditis, congenital heart disease and congenital or acquired structural abnormalities.

**Clinical application:** In a patient with established heart failure who suddenly deteriorates, look for precipitating factors such as infection, medication non-adherence, arrhythmia, anaemia, renal impairment and acute coronary syndrome.

items.text: Primary hypertension: no single identifiable underlying cause.
Secondary hypertension: identifiable underlying disease or exposure.

blocks.text: Other important causes include dehydration, adrenal crisis, medication effects and severe arrhythmias.
**Exam pearl:** Hypotension accompanied by altered consciousness, cold extremities, oliguria or poor peripheral perfusion should raise concern for shock.

items.text: **L** – Low blood glucose (a mimic of syncope)

blocks.text: **Clinical application:** Syncope during exertion, while supine, or associated with palpitations or a family history of sudden cardiac death warrants urgent cardiac assessment.

items.text: **R** – Response to stress, anxiety or stimulants
**T** – Tachycardia from systemic causes (fever, anaemia, dehydration)

blocks.text: Other causes include caffeine, alcohol, nicotine and certain medications.
Remember that tachycardia can be physiological, compensatory or pathological.

items.text: **O** – Overdose of rate-limiting drugs (beta-blockers, digoxin, some calcium-channel blockers)

blocks.text: Additional causes include hypothermia, raised intracranial pressure, inferior myocardial infarction and electrolyte disturbances, particularly hyperkalaemia.
**Exam pearl:** An irregularly irregular pulse is classically associated with atrial fibrillation. Confirm with a 12-lead ECG.

items.text: **W** – Water hammer pulse from aortic regurgitation

blocks.text: Other causes include thyrotoxicosis, severe anaemia, pregnancy and patent ductus arteriosus.

items.text: **K** – Kinetic impairment of cardiac output (e.g. cardiogenic shock)

blocks.text: Also associated with patent ductus arteriosus and other high-output states.
**Definition:** An inspiratory fall in systolic blood pressure greater than 10 mmHg.

blocks.title: Think of severe ventricular dysfunction, especially:

blocks.text: It is characterised by alternating strong and weak arterial pulses despite a regular heart rhythm.
Also consider constrictive pericarditis and superior vena cava obstruction (which causes venous congestion, although the JVP waveform may be absent or difficult to assess).
Other causes include deep vein thrombosis, medications such as calcium-channel blockers and malnutrition.

items.text: **H** – Heart disease, especially cyanotic congenital heart disease

blocks.text: Distinguish central cyanosis from peripheral cyanosis during clinical examination.
Other causes include bronchiectasis, cystic fibrosis and hypertrophic osteoarthropathy.
For OSCE, remember the four main valve lesions:
Remember that an enlarged cardiac silhouette on chest X-ray does not always mean true chamber enlargement; pericardial effusion and technical factors can contribute.
Other causes include post-myocardial infarction syndromes, trauma, radiation and post-cardiac surgery.
**Exam pearl:** In Nigeria, tuberculosis is an important cause to consider in unexplained pericardial effusion.
**Clinical features – BECK'S TRIAD**
Other findings include tachycardia, pulsus paradoxus and reduced cardiac output.

items.text: **T** – Transvenous devices and injection drug use

blocks.text: Other important organisms include coagulase-negative staphylococci, particularly in prosthetic valve infection.
**Exam pearl:** Staphylococcus aureus is an important cause of acute infective endocarditis. Viridans streptococci are classically associated with subacute disease.

subsections.subsection_title: 24. Risk factors for ischaemic heart disease

blocks.text: Additional important risk factors include family history of premature cardiovascular disease and chronic kidney disease.
Also remember diabetes, chronic kidney disease, obesity and family history.

Other causes include pregnancy-associated cardiomyopathy, chemotherapy, myocarditis and nutritional deficiencies.

items.text: **R** – Rupture or other catastrophic structural disease

blocks.text: Other causes include severe aortic stenosis, myocarditis, pulmonary embolism and congenital coronary abnormalities.
**C** - **Cardiogenic shock**
Pump failure: myocardial infarction, severe cardiomyopathy, serious arrhythmias.
**O** - **Obstructive shock**
Mechanical obstruction: cardiac tamponade, massive pulmonary embolism, tension pneumothorax.
**D** - **Distributive shock**
Abnormal vascular tone: septic, anaphylactic and neurogenic shock.
**A** - **Absolute volume loss (hypovolaemic shock)**
Haemorrhage, dehydration, burns and gastrointestinal fluid loss.

items.text: **P** – Papillary muscle or ventricular septal rupture

blocks.text: Other causes include severe valvular disease and advanced cardiomyopathy.

items.text: **E** – Extrinsic cardiac or great vessel obstruction

blocks.text: These are primarily reversible causes considered during cardiac arrest assessment, rather than an exhaustive list of all arrhythmia causes.
Also consider connective tissue disorders, carcinoid disease and papillary muscle dysfunction.

items.text: **N** – Neonatal and congenital heart disease-associated pulmonary hypertension

blocks.title: For formal examination purposes, use the five WHO pulmonary hypertension groups:

items.text: Pulmonary hypertension due to left heart disease.
Pulmonary hypertension due to lung disease and/or hypoxia.
Pulmonary hypertension due to pulmonary artery obstruction.
Pulmonary hypertension with unclear or multifactorial mechanisms.

blocks.text: Examples:

rows: Immobilisation, prolonged bed rest, heart failure
Cancer, pregnancy, oral contraceptives, inherited thrombophilia

blocks.text: **Clinical pearl:** A pulmonary embolism may present with sudden dyspnoea, pleuritic chest pain, tachycardia, hypoxaemia or syncope. A normal chest X-ray does not exclude it.

items.text: **STEMI:** When indicated, particularly when timely primary PCI cannot be delivered.
**Acute ischaemic stroke:** In eligible patients within the appropriate time window after brain imaging excludes haemorrhage.
**High-risk pulmonary embolism:** With haemodynamic instability, when appropriate and not contraindicated.
